summary:
# NOTES: *Cole of Spyglass Mountain* (Arthur Preston Hankins, 1923)

Single book, no multiple volumes. Chapters I–XXXIV.

## CHARACTERS
- **Joshua Cole** (protagonist; "Cole"; later "Tony"; "Fifty-six thirty-five"/"56-35" in House of Refuge; "Cole of Spyglass Mountain"). Black hair, gray-blue eyes, Grecian nose, ascetic face, age 14 at start, ~20–21 at end. Loves astronomy, slugs, stars.
- **Lester Cole**: younger brother (11→13 in text; ~13 at start, Joshua says "about thirteen"). Black hair. Turns on Joshua; later works in shoe store; birthday June 15 (21st birthday).
- **John Cole**: father, traveling hardware salesman, drinker, gambler (ponies), fast women; drowns sons in tub. Cruel.
- **Blanche Florence Cole**: mother, from old Maryland family (came with Lord Calvert). Dies in Hathaway while Joshua at House of Refuge.
- **Silvanus Madmallet** ("Ole Madhouse," "Ole Hothatchet," "Ole Sorehammer"): tyrannical teacher; expels Joshua with poker standoff.
- **Slinky Dawson**: teacher's pet, delivers note; Joshua extorts it.
- **Spud Mulligan, "Did" Eustace**: gang friends.
- **Zida Hunt**: negro cook/maid, friend.
- **Ambrose**: former stable man for Coles (gave info to Mundy).
- **Madge Mundy** ("Shanty Madge," "gypo queen"): bronze-gold frizzly hair, Oriental-topaz / reddish-brown eyes, Pocahontas coloring. Age 11 at meeting, 18 later.
- **George "Bloodmop" Mundy**: red-haired gypo man, dies ~3 months before story's Spur scene; sky-blue eyes, wife's husband. Calls Joshua "kid."
- **Elizabeth "'Lizabeth" Mundy**: Madge's mother, refined, Blanche's contemporary, dark hair, from Maryland-like refined background.
- **Dickinson**: big plainclothes detective; sympathetic.
- **Sergeant**; **police judge** (fat, blond, blue eyes).
- **Beaver Clegg**: House of Refuge Juvenile Dept head; ugly, Lincoln-like; variable star observer with 3-inch refractor; teaches astronomy on roof; dies of heart failure; left Joshua telescope, books, photographs.
- **Superintendent** (unnamed; grandson-of-founder detail). **Peter D. Florence**: founder of House of Refuge, Joshua's grandfather. **Peter Henry Florence**: uncle, Virginia, wealthy, died later; will left Joshua $150,000 at age 21 (contingent; changed to Lester if Joshua not found).
- **Felix Wolfgang ("Slim Wolfgang," "Number 23-44")**: Norwegian, freckled, sandy hair, gangster, gambler, freckled "egg of a guinea hen." Shot Joshua. Hired Whimperer to track him. Girl: **Winnie the Weeper**.
- **The Whimperer ("De Whimperer," "Whimp," John Yegg)**: pitted scar on cheek (acid-made), twisted mouth, fake arm dislocations, whimpermeter poems; stole telescope, sold for $100. Jocker.
- **California Bill Fox ("Bill," "Cali")**: 53, stage driver turned six-mule freighter; slate-gray eyes, black eyebrows, ex-deputy sheriff Chaparral County; "character"; named Joshua "Cole of Spyglass Mountain" and "Tony"; fatalist; "hi-yu skookum"; "cultus."
- **Jack Montgomery**: brown-haired, Eastern-college, son of Montgomery of Montgomery & Applegate; suitor; later marries Madge.
- **Lee Sweet**: owner of Box-R Ranch; huge, red-faced, leonine whiskers; drunk; shoots at Joshua's cabin; set by Slim.
- **Jawbone Mahoney**: Irish boss-powderman; drunk, fired shot causing slide.
- **Demarest** (Philip, "Heavens to Betsy"), **Spruce**, **Tillou**: contractors Demarest, Spruce and Tillou.
- **Bluenose**: fellow hammerman, cut Joshua's hair.
- **Dr. J. Miles Stanhope**: drunk Ragtown doctor, Van Dyke beard, roulette, Gladys.
- **Emanuel Peters, Branscomb**: engineers.
- **Mary Montgomery**: Jack's sister.
- **Dr. Hiram A. Buck**: Milton University director (Elmfield, Mass.). **Dr. Emanuel Schlott**: German telescopist who confirms photo.
- **Mr. Golden**: G-string mining engineer; helped survey.
- **Mr. Smiley**: homesteader.

## PLACES
- Hathaway (city); Grant Avenue (Coles' house, No. 355); Park Avenue (earlier home); Crescent Rink; Hathaway's Boyland; Third-room Nine; Madmallet's school; vacant swampy lot with slug.
- House of Refuge (reformatory; wings; Juvenile Dept; roof observatory).
- Gypo camp near railroad tracks; Spur (desert railhead, Cal.); Box-R Ranch; Wild Woman Springs; Yucca Flat; Cactus Slope; Hairpin Curve; Shirt-tail Bend; Bobcat Point; Gonzales Wells; Seven Palms; G-string (mining town, Saddle Mountain); Stirrup Lake; Saddle Mountain; Caldron Cañon; Buttonhook Bend; Ragtown (tent town; The Silver Dollar, The Golden Eagle, Scotty's, Palace Dance Hall, etc.); Camp One/Two; Hill of Springs; Spyglass Mountain (Joshua's, ~1000 ft above lake, summit ~7,750 ft); Los Angeles (Federal Building land office); Sacramento, Oakland bar.

## KEY EVENTS (in order)
1. **Ch I**: Slug on chip (*Limax Campestris*) bet; Madmallet punishes Lester; Joshua threatens him with iron poker; "I won't set down."
2. **Ch II**: Madmallet's feud (Proctor's *Other Worlds Than Ours*, Darwin, Huxley); Joshua expelled; Lester suspended a week; Joshua takes father's razor; slug walks razor edge; plan to intercept Slinky Dawson's note.
3. **Ch III**: Father's ducking; Joshua's plan to go West; Slinky surrenders note ("Mrs. John H. Cole, Three fifty-five Grant Avenue"); Joshua meets Madge Mundy at Crescent Rink (reddish-golden hair, topaz eyes).
4. **Ch IV**: Teaches Madge skating; she is gypo queen; father "Bloodmop" Mundy; plan to go West; Spud sent to check Lester; Lester went home.
5. **Ch V**: Sleeps in boxcar; walks to camp; breakfast with Mundys; Mrs. Mundy's interest; Bloodmop says he'll think about a job.
6. **Ch VI**: Bloodmop's talk with wife (Joshua's background; cops hunting him); Joshua and Madge stargazing (Orion, Big Dipper, Pointer, Pole Star, Argo quote); detective Dickinson arrests him with razor.
7. **Ch VII**: Dickinson warns father; John Cole takes Joshua to hardware stores, then police court; judge commits Joshua to House of Refuge until 21 (seven years); Dickinson's advice: "Don't fight back."
8. **Ch VIII**: House of Refuge; superintendent learns Joshua is grandson of Peter D. Florence; "Number 5635" (Fifty-six thirty-five); Beaver Clegg (ugly, Lincoln-like) takes him in; Clegg's astronomy/variable stars.
9. **Ch IX**: Night roof lessons with telescope (Mars/moon, Clavius, Tycho, Blancanus); Joshua called "Tony"; T-and-H medal; harassment; fight with Number 23-44 (Felix Wolfgang) who spat in his face.
10. **Ch X**: Fight; Joshua deliberately breaks record to avoid parole; birch/bamboo whipping; second medal; mother dies; Uncle Peter Henry Florence visits; Clegg dies; Joshua pardoned at 20; Lester (shoe store) refuses help; Joshua runs off by boxcar; Wolfgang on same train.
11. **Ch XI**: Pittsburgh; brakeman; Joshua lectures with telescope at village; meets The Whimperer, a John Yegg, who offers partnership.
12. **Ch XII**: Whimpermeter poem; "lump" and "set-down" lingo; Wolfgang & Whimperer conspire (Wolfgang pays $5).
13. **Ch XIII**: Whimperer plots; freight rides; Kansas; Whimperer steals telescope at night ($500 value), sells for $100.
14. **Ch XIV**: Philosophy of tramp life; slug meditation in southern Colorado; Joshua prays.
15. **Ch XV**: Spur, Gold Belt Cut-off railroad; Demarest, Spruce & Tillou contractors; California Bill Fox; Bloodmop dead; Madge "Shanty Madge" boss.
16. **Ch XVI**: Ride up San Antonio range; Bill names him "Tony" and "Cole of Spyglass Mountain"; Stirrup Lake.
17. **Ch XVII**: Camp One; Joshua reunites with Madge; clothes bought ($17.35); meets Mrs. Mundy; plans telescope and cave; Spyglass Mountain idea; "Is there any money in it?"
18. **Ch XVIII**: Tunnel in Hill of Springs; Jawbone; Ragtown; Bill's homestead idea.
19. **Ch XIX**: Golden helps survey; land office in LA; buys telescope parts; Ragtown: meets Whimperer (skeleton game), chases him into Slim Wolfgang's tent; warning about Jawbone's drunken shot causing slide.
20. **Ch XX**: Mrs. Mundy's homestead plan (Joshua advises filing in her name); Joshua shot by rifle at dusk on trail.
21. **Ch XXI**: Joshua in Ragtown hospital (Dr. Stanhope); Madge says she's through; land claim allowed.
22. **Ch XXII**: Joshua's plan: coyote hole around slide; Demarest pays $5,000; Joshua declines job; mentions Mars (Mar 18 June opposition).
23. **Ch XXIII**: Madge, Mrs. Mundy, Joshua discuss Mars canals theory; Jack Montgomery arrives.
24. **Ch XXIV**: Joshua buys 8-inch telescope ($2,000) and saddle; horse Argo (dapple gray; "Prince" renamed); well; Mundys move; Lee Sweet confronts; Bill's "hypocrite" talk; Wolfgang watches.
25. **Ch XXV**: Campfire; Joshua proposes; Madge says she loves Jack's money; Joshua recites O'Reilly "dreamer lives forever."
26. **Ch XXVI**: Bill's "moron" lecture; Whimperer arrives drunk on wagon.
27. **Ch XXVII**: Whimperer confesses: stole telescope, Slim hired him to spy, Slim shot Joshua with .30-30; Joshua gives $10; Whimperer leaves on stage.
28. **Ch XXVIII**: Slim receives Whimperer's letter; Winnie the Weeper; Joshua builds trail, observatory; "You'll come back to Spyglass Mountain."
29. **Ch XXIX**: Winter; Joshua's articles (*The Universe*, *American Astronomer*, *Journal of Astronomy* "Cole of Spyglass Mountain"); reports Eratosthenes vegetation; Lee Sweet's hostility.
30. **Ch XXX**: Slim explains conspiracy to Winnie (father John Cole's plot; Peter Henry Florence's will; $25,000 to Slim); Sweet used to harass Joshua.
31. **Ch XXXI**: Madge says she and mother go to LA (Montgomerys); Sweet fires at Joshua's cabin from shelf; Madge questions his courage.
32. **Ch XXXII**: Madge's letter ending engagement to Jack; Bill mediates; Bill confronts Slim and Winnie in tent; Slim plans East trip.
33. **Ch XXXIII**: Joshua alone on night of June 15 (Lester's 21st birthday); Mars observation; Bill brings Slim, who confesses.
34. **Ch XXXIV**: Joshua forgives Slim; Bill almost kicks him, lets him go; Bill rides to find Sweet; June 18 Joshua sees Mars figure at 12:10; photographs; shot by Lee Sweet's men; telegram to Milton University (Dr. Buck); Madge returns; Joshua vindicated by Dr. Emanuel Schlott's photograph; ends with Joshua and Madge together.
